items.title: The rank of a smooth map at a point
Immersions, submersions, and constant-rank maps
Regular and critical points and values
The immersion and submersion loci are open
The smooth inverse function theorem on manifolds
items.strategy: Choose source and target charts about the point and its image, reduce to the Euclidean inverse function theorem at the coordinate representative, and then import the higher-regularity local-inverse result before transporting the local inverse back through the charts.

items.title: The constant-rank theorem for manifolds
items.strategy: Work in charts around the chosen source and target points, use the chain rule and chart diffeomorphisms to show the coordinate representative has the same constant rank, apply the Euclidean constant-rank normal form, and transport the resulting slice model back to the manifolds.

items.title: Local normal form for immersions
Local normal form for submersions
Every immersion is locally an embedding
Every submersion is an open map
A smooth map of locally maximal rank has locally constant rank
items.strategy: Transfer the map to a chart representative. If the rank at the chosen point equals the maximum rank on a neighborhood, lower semicontinuity of the Euclidean differential rank forces the same rank on a smaller neighborhood, and chart invariance carries that conclusion back to the manifold.

items.title: Embedded submanifolds and slice charts
Slice-chart restrictions form a smooth atlas
items.strategy: Restrict each slice chart to the coordinate slice and compute the transition maps by composing ambient chart transitions with the coordinate inclusion and projection. The same description shows that the restricted charts generate exactly the subspace topology, not merely a coarser one.

items.title: Smooth embeddings
The smooth structure of an embedded submanifold is unique
items.strategy: Use the slice-chart atlas from the previous lemma and show that any smooth structure making the inclusion an embedding has the same local coordinates: every admissible chart must be smoothly compatible with the slice coordinates because both identify the same subset with the same coordinate slice.

items.title: The inclusion of an embedded submanifold is a smooth embedding
The image of a smooth embedding is an embedded submanifold
items.strategy: Apply the immersion normal form near each source point to identify the map locally with a coordinate inclusion. The homeomorphism-onto-its-image condition then lets the ambient neighborhood be shrunk so that no other sheet re-enters, producing genuine slice charts on the image.

items.title: An injective immersion from a compact manifold is an embedding
items.strategy: A smooth map is continuous, so an injective immersion from a compact manifold to a Hausdorff manifold is a continuous bijection onto its image. The compact-to-Hausdorff theorem makes that corestriction a homeomorphism, and local embedding was already proved for immersions.

items.title: Immersed submanifolds
Smoothness into an embedded submanifold is an initial property
items.strategy: Work in slice charts for the codomain. The corestriction is smooth exactly when its coordinate representatives in the slice coordinates are smooth, and those are obtained from the ambient coordinates by deleting the zero normal coordinates.

items.title: Smoothness of a map on an embedded submanifold is local in the ambient space
Codimension and hypersurfaces
Local defining maps for embedded submanifolds
Embedded submanifolds admit local defining submersions
items.strategy: In a slice chart, take the normal coordinate projection as the defining map. Its differential is the coordinate projection onto the normal factor, hence surjective, and its zero fibre is exactly the coordinate slice.

items.title: A regular level set is an embedded submanifold
items.strategy: At each point of the fiber, the map is a submersion, so the manifold submersion normal form gives coordinates in which the fiber is the zero slice. Those slice charts patch to the embedded-submanifold structure, and the codimension is the target dimension.

items.title: The tangent space of a regular level set is the kernel
items.strategy: Use the local submersion normal form for the defining map. In those coordinates the level set is the coordinate slice and the differential is the coordinate projection, so the tangent vectors are exactly the ones with zero normal component, hence exactly the kernel.

items.title: The preimage theorem for submanifolds under submersions
items.strategy: Give the target submanifold a local defining submersion, compose it with the ambient submersion, and apply the regular-level-set theorem to the composite. The tangent-space formula then comes from the kernel description of the regular level set together with the defining-map kernel for the target submanifold.

items.title: The diagonal is an embedded submanifold
items.strategy: Use product charts on M times M and pass from coordinates (u,v) to (u,v-u). In those coordinates the diagonal is exactly the zero slice in the second factor, so it is embedded and its tangent space is the diagonal subspace.

items.title: The graph of a smooth map is an embedded submanifold
items.strategy: Form the smooth map G from M times N to N times N given by (p,q) mapped to (F(p),q). The graph is the preimage of the diagonal, and a local defining submersion for the diagonal composes with G to a local defining submersion for the graph because the second factor contributes the identity in the normal directions.

items.title: Transverse intersections of coordinate slices have the expected local form
items.strategy: Inside one coordinate chart, combine the two independent normal-coordinate projections into one submersion to a product Euclidean space. The common slice is then the zero fiber of that combined projection, so it is again a coordinate slice of codimension equal to the sum of the two codimensions.

items.title: A discrete embedded submanifold is locally closed and countable
items.strategy: A zero-dimensional slice chart identifies the submanifold locally with the single point in R^0, hence with a closed subset of the ambient chart domain. As a discrete subspace of a second-countable manifold it is itself second countable, so its singleton basis is countable.

items.title: An injective immersion need not be an embedding
The image of every immersion need not be an embedded submanifold
A regular value need not belong to the image
Rank at one point need not determine nearby rank
An embedded submanifold need not be open in the ambient manifold
The intrinsic topology of an immersed submanifold need not be the subspace topology

title: Rank Theorems and Embedded Submanifolds — Examples

items.title: Coordinate inclusions are immersions and coordinate projections are submersions
The special linear group is a codimension-one embedded submanifold
items.strategy: View determinant as a smooth map on the matrix space. At a matrix A with determinant 1, differentiate det(A(I+tA^{-1}H)) at t=0 to obtain the linear functional H mapped to tr(A^{-1}H), which is surjective because it sends A to n. The regular-level-set theorem then identifies SL(n,R) as the fiber over 1.

items.title: A cylinder is the preimage of a circle under a projection
items.strategy: Take the projection pi from R^3 to R^2, (x,y,z) mapped to (x,y), and the unit circle S^1 subset R^2 as the regular level set of x^2+y^2. The projection is a submersion, so its preimage of S^1 is S^1 times R, an embedded submanifold by the preimage theorem.

items.title: The graph of the sine function is an embedded submanifold
A value outside the image can still be regular
items.strategy: For f(x)=e^x on R, the fiber over 0 is empty while the derivative is never zero. The regular-value definition is therefore satisfied vacuously at 0, even though 0 is not attained.

items.title: A figure-eight curve is an immersed image but not an embedded submanifold
items.strategy: Use the immersion t mapped to (sin t,sin 2t) from R to R^2. Its derivative never vanishes, but the image crosses itself at the origin, so no neighborhood of the crossing has the subspace topology of a one-manifold.

items.title: Countably many concentric circles give an injective immersion that is not an embedding
items.strategy: Let M be the disjoint union of one copy of the unit circle and one copy of each circle of radius 1+1/n for n at least 1. Each component includes smoothly into R^2, and the componentwise map is injective and immersive. Its image is the union of those concentric circles, where every neighborhood of a point on the unit circle meets infinitely many outer circles, so the unit-circle component is not open in the subspace topology even though it is open in the disjoint-union source.

items.title: A rank drop at one point need not persist locally
items.strategy: For f(x)=x^2 on R, the derivative is zero at the origin and nonzero at every nonzero point. Thus the rank at 0 does not determine the nearby rank behavior.
